name: Infuse accumulates 10% of group damage, absorbs healing, and unleashes the stored amount as Shadow damage (#509)
contract: Infuse 681403 (SpellFamilyName 26, Shadow, 40 yd, 30 s cooldown, health cost 35% of base mana) is a 10 s
debuff (DurationIndex 1) whose effect 0 is SPELL_AURA_DUMMY with EffectTriggerSpell 681404 and whose
effect 1 is SPELL_AURA_SCHOOL_ABSORB with MiscValue 127 (all schools); 681404 has one
SPELL_EFFECT_SCHOOL_DAMAGE effect targeting an enemy area of radius 10 yards with MaxAffectedTargets 1.
The healer stands 30 yards from the victim, within 40-yard healing range, so only the victim competes for
the damage hit. The client's own cast description reads \"Accumulates damage dealt to the target by you,
your party or raid members, and their minions for $d, then unleashes the stored amount as Shadow
damage.\" and the debuff's unit-frame tooltip reads \"Accumulating damage dealt by the caster's group at
diminishing rates; unleashes the stored amount when this effect expires.\". No rate is given by the
client data, so the only original number is the talent text of the same ability (Conquest of Azeroth
Fleshweaver tree, node 7434): \"Accumulates 10% of all damage dealt to the target and unleashes it after
10 seconds, dealing Shadow damage and absorbing healing done to the target equal to the damage done for
10 seconds. Damage dealt is unable to exceed 3 times your maximum health.\" That is what this scenario
measures: damage the target takes from the caster and the caster's party or raid members (and their
minions) adds 10% of its value to a pool stored on the aura, capped at three times the caster's maximum
health; the pool is mirrored into the absorb effect's amount so the unit frame shows it and healing done
to the target is absorbed by it; on expiry the pool is cast through 681404 as its base points, which the
core resolves to exactly that amount because 681404's own bonus multiplier is zero and it has no spell
bonus entry. The heal absorb is measured comparatively: auto-attack swings leave a pool far smaller than
the 32-38 point heal used here, so the heal must land for less than the first one did (the cumulative
healing total stays under 1.9 times the control heal instead of the doubling seen without an absorb),
while the pool snapshot proves the stored amount and the absorb capacity agree exactly. NOT asserted
here: party/raid membership of the damaging unit (the scenario damages with the caster itself), the
three-times-maximum-health cap (the pool stays far below it), the \"diminishing rates\" wording of the
debuff tooltip (the original data gives no rate behind it, so none was invented), and whether a dispelled
or dead-target debuff should still explode (only AURA_REMOVE_BY_EXPIRE unleashes).

Infuse pays 35% of base mana as health; keep the caster well above it
Injure the victim so heals are effective, not overheal
A small heal whose size the pool easily covers once damage is stored
CONTROL: heal the victim before Infuse
CONTROL: the heal lands
CONTROL: cumulative healing on the victim
Infuse the victim
Infuse lands as a debuff
The debuff lasts ten seconds
SETUP: nothing is stored yet
SETUP: no heal absorb yet
Auto-attacks are the controlled damage source inside the window
SETUP: the swings hit the victim
SETUP: the debuff survived the damage
Damage dealt to the victim while Infuse was active
DISCRIMINATING: the pool is 10% of the damage the victim took
The stored amount
DISCRIMINATING: the heal absorb capacity equals the damage done
Nothing explodes before expiry
Re-injure so the second heal is effective if it lands at all
Heal the victim while the pool is up
The second heal is cast
DISCRIMINATING: healing done to the target is absorbed by the damage done
SETUP: the debuff expires after its ten seconds
DISCRIMINATING: the stored amount is unleashed once when the debuff expires
DISCRIMINATING: the unleash deals the stored amount as Shadow damage
The debuff is gone after the unleash
The caster survived the health cost
The victim survived
